speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The draft Bill on the first set of amendments was released for public consultation from 1 to 18 March 2016.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) has evaluated all the feedback received and, where relevant, accepted the suggestions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The first, in relation to the implementation of the CRS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Singapore is firmly committed to upholding internationally accepted standards for the exchange of information under the CRS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Members might recall that in 2014, the Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax purposes, of which Singapore is a member, and the Group of 20 (G20) major economies, endorsed automatic exchange of information (AEOI) under the CRS as a global standard, and asked all members to commit to a timeline of 2018 or earlier for implementation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The CRS sets out the financial account information to be exchanged, the financial institutions (FIs) required to report, the different types of accounts and taxpayers covered as well as the customer due diligence procedures to be followed by FIs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Singapore had announced in November 2014 that we would implement the CRS to commence AEOI by 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: To date, more than 90 jurisdictions, including major financial centres, such as Dubai, Hong Kong, Luxembourg and Switzerland, have also endorsed the CRS and committed to implementation timelines of 2017 or 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The proposed amendments in this Bill will enable FIs to put in place necessary processes and systems to collect CRS information from 1 January 2017, in order to meet our timeline to commence first exchange of information under the CRS in 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Clauses 4 and 5 of the Bill make amendments in relation to existing provisions in the Income Tax Act, which had previously been introduced in 2013 to implement the Singapore-United States Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act Inter-governmental Agreement (FATCA IGA).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The provisions introduced in 2013 provide the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) the necessary information-gathering powers to fulfil Singapore's role in facilitating FATCA-compliance under the Inter-Governmental Agreement (IGA).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: These powers include the routine collection and transmission of relevant information as well as enforcement powers to sanction non-compliance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The amendments in this Bill make clear that these existing provisions are also applicable to any other AEOI agreement that is in accordance with the CRS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: This will enable Singapore to sign Competent Authority Agreements (CAAs) with other jurisdictions to implement AEOI under the CRS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Second, the amendments in clause 8 empower FIs to collect and retain the CRS information for all non-Singapore tax residents, instead of only from tax residents of jurisdictions with which Singapore has an AEOI agreement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The Wider Approach is an effective approach preferred by our FIs because it removes the need for them to repeatedly review whether the accounts are reportable each time Singapore enters into a new Competent Authority Agreement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The Wider Approach has been adopted by many jurisdictions, such as the United Kingdom (UK), Sweden, Japan and Korea.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Clause 9 of the Bill provides for this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The amendments also ensure effective implementation of the CRS, including vesting in IRAS the necessary administrative powers to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The changes include mandating the electronic filing of returns and information and are provided for in clauses 2, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 of the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Next, Madam, I will deal with the changes to the Productivity and Innovation Credit (PIC) scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: These were announced in the 2016 Budget Statement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The PIC changes are provided for in clauses 2 and 3 of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I will focus my speech on the Productivity and Innovation Credit (PIC) Scheme.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The PIC scheme was introduced to encourage productivity and innovation activities in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It provides support to businesses that make investments to improve their productivity.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is no doubt that the PIC scheme has been a success.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, as with any scheme, there are bound to be loopholes and people are bound to try and exploit and abuse the scheme.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While the percentage requiring clawback seems low, it does represent a significant number of people trying to cheat the system or submitting inaccurate claims, perhaps unintentionally, and $11 million does seem like a sizable amount of money.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Quite clearly, if we investigate and audit the remaining 70% of claims, we will uncover even more cases and have to claw back even more funds.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But what alarms me more are the other figures published in a The Straits Times' article, and I quote, "IRAS has rejected or clawed back the sums paid out to about one in three cash payout claims filed by the self-employed as the claims were inaccurate or false.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Either way, this $358 million figure points to a real need to strengthen the system.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While we are phasing out the PIC scheme, I understand that, on the ground, PIC consultants are going all out, doing whatever it is possible to source for clients and make as many claims as possible and whilst stocks last.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This makes it even more important for us to strengthen the system and strengthen it in the right way.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The fact is that many people are still trying their luck.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We need to strengthen the system so that fewer people want to even try their luck.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We need to strengthen the approval process and make sure people know that it is being strengthened.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We need to urgently investigate and audit more claims.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We need to send a deterrent message to companies that if they try to cheat the system, they will get caught and the penalties are severe.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We need to increase the odds significantly and the current odds are in favour of the cheaters as there is only about a one in three chance of their claim being audited.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will the Ministry also consider cutting down on providing grants to low productivity yield projects like websites or app designs?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And will the Ministry consider giving out the grants in disbursements for innovation projects that need to show payoff, in terms of productivity gains and projection of sales?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: All of which requires information filing one year from implementation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We also need to take a stronger stand when it comes to PIC consultants.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A PIC consultant is a person or a business entity that provides advice or assistance to businesses on PIC matters for a fee.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A PIC consultant is expected to be knowledgeable about the PIC scheme and be familiar with the correct procedures when submitting PIC cash payout claims for his clients.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am sure we have all seen their claims and guarantees of cashing in on the PIC scheme and I have met numerous residents telling me stories of how they have been approached by the consultants.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We need to make changes to ensure that consultants are no longer able to cheat the Government and also the companies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The amendment in the Bill requiring the use of the electronic service is a step forward.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It will help end the abuse of the system where companies sign blank PIC forms and pass them to the consultants.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As we now streamline the application process, I question the need for PIC consultants to submit the application forms on behalf of their clients or applicants.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Ministry clarify why we continue to allow this and whether there are plans to phase this out?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I appreciate that some companies need help for PIC matters.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But can IRAS not handle these enquiries directly?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: IRAS already states on its website that companies can contact them for assistance or clarification on PIC matters.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There are even separate phone numbers for companies and the self-employed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And if the enquiry contains confidential information, they can email IRAS via myTax Mail for added security.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: With all these in place, is there a need for consultants to help provide advice and submit applications?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I ask that this be reviewed also because I have met residents at my Meet-the-People Sessions who have been cheated by the consultants.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, I am more concerned that as we get closer and closer to the end date, more and more people will try to cash in.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This Bill does help to strengthen the system.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I sincerely believe that we need to do more.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: According to Oxfam International, lost tax revenue from money salted away offshore costs governments more than $150 billion a year.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This is estimated to be enough to eliminate extreme poverty across the globe twice over.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I commend the Singapore Government for its strong efforts in the anti-money laundering regime and its active cooperation with other jurisdictions through the exchange of information for tax purposes to facilitate tax compliance.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The way forward will be difficult and will require us to navigate obstacles with great skill, cleverness and caution.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: First, we should be mindful of the impact of CRS on Singapore's competitiveness as an international financial centre.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Many industry participants are concerned that an overly enthusiastic response at this early implementation stage, imposing more than the required obligations on Financial Institutions (FIs) may hurt the competitiveness and growth of our wealth management industry.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: It is important to observe the pace adopted by other jurisdictions and consider a measured approach at a prudent pace.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Not all countries have signed up, and those which have signed may implement Competent Authority Agreements (CAAs) at a different pace.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Could the Minister share the impact on Singapore's competitiveness if other financial centres adopt a different approach?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: How can we ensure a level playing field among all major financial centres, including Dubai, Hong Kong, Luxembourg and Switzerland, to minimise regulatory arbitrage?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: To avoid FIs being overwhelmed by the administrative burden of CRS implementation and the complexity of system enhancements, they will need clear guidance to enable a consistent interpretation of requirements.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The industry expects the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to issue guidance notes that set a reasonable industry standard that strives to balance responsible global compliance with reasonable expectations of responses from FIs.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Burdensome complexity brings with it the risk of non-compliance and its accompanying cost of penalties.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: For example, it is common for FI clients to maintain multiple residences or they may travel so frequently that they have no tax residency status.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Another example is how will information that Singapore receives on offshore income of Singapore resident taxpayers be used, collected and shared?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Different FIs may hold differing reading of the same individual's tax status.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister how we could take a more nuanced approach that would provide greater clarity for industry players to deal with issues of tax residency.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: FIs should be expected to do the necessary due diligence to establish the clients' tax residency.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: But, to a large extent, FIs will have to rely on their clients' declarations or what their clients declare to them.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Is that good enough, or will the FIs be expected to corroborate those declarations, and how far are they expected to go to do so?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: To what extent will FIs be culpable for inaccurate declarations?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Third, we must ensure that a robust process is in place to determine the readiness of bilateral partners of CAAs before bilateral information exchanges commence.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Not every country is as ready as we are to deal with transparency, and we have a duty to the clients we serve to safeguard their privacy against abuse.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Tax information can be misused for a variety of nefarious ends, including criminal enterprise, political corruption and social chaos.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: We have heard of cases where tax information is misused to achieve political objectives or leaked to criminals.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Also, how do we ensure there is full reciprocity with AEOI partners in terms of information exchanged?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Even if we do all this well, it is still important for us to communicate skillfully and clearly to international clients who bank in Singapore how rigorously we will safeguard their interests, so that they are assured that their information will not fall into the wrong hands.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: One input that the Government may consider referencing is published corruption indices by independent international organisations, such as Transparency International, which will be well-known to all stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Last but not least, Madam, with the advent of information exchanges for tax compliance, we need clarity on an individual's right to privacy protection under our laws.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: In this, wealth managers can be the authorities' greatest allies in educating and advising their clients, to bring them on board, and we should work together towards a common cause.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Foo Mee Har raised three points: the protection of taxpayers' confidentiality and considerations for the Singapore Government when determining AEOI partners; second, ensuring a level playing field with competitor jurisdictions, such as Switzerland and Hong Kong; and third, whether there will be more detailed guidance provided to the FIs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: First, and as pointed out by Ms Foo Mee Har, there must be a level playing field amongst all major financial centres, including Hong Kong and Switzerland, to minimise regulatory arbitrage.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These financial centres have endorsed AEOI under the common reporting standard and are committed to implementation timelines of 2017 or 2018.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Second, and as also highlighted by Ms Foo, it is critical that we protect taxpayers' confidentiality.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is why we will engage in AEOI only with jurisdictions that have strong rule of law and the ability to ensure the confidentiality of information exchanged and prevent its unauthorised use.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: CRS includes specific rules on confidentiality and data safeguards that must be in place before information is exchanged.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax Purposes has also set up an expert panel to review jurisdictions' implementation of these safeguards to ensure that AEOI takes place in a secure environment.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Singapore will take into consideration the outcome of such reviews when we consider which jurisdictions to engage in AEOI with.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Third, there must be full reciprocity with AEOI partners in terms of information exchanged.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These conditions are necessary to make sure that we continue to respect the legitimate expectations for confidentiality even as we implement AEOI to contribute to the global effort to tackle offshore tax evasion.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We are mindful that implementing AEOI under the CRS will impose new obligations on our FIs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: FIs will need to institute new procedures and configure their systems to fulfil their customer due diligence and reporting obligations under the CRS.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Government is working closely with the financial industry in our implementation of the CRS.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MOF, IRAS and MAS held a public consultation on proposed legislative amendments in March and will be releasing draft regulations for consultation by June this year.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This will allow FIs to have sufficient time to make changes to their procedures and systems to comply with the CRS requirements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The regulations will detail the CRS requirements that FIs have to comply with.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Moving on to Mr Louis Ng's speech on the PIC, we agree with Mr Ng on the need to ensure that PIC claims are genuine and in order.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: IRAS has taken and will continue to take a strong stance against abuse of the PIC scheme, whether consultants are involved or not.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: IRAS does not make it mandatory for taxpayers to submit PIC claims through consultants, and many businesses submitted the applications on their own without the help of consultants.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: At the end of the day, it is the company's choice as to whether to use consultants or not.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But from our perspective, we would require that any information that they submit for their claims must be true and accurate.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Ng noted that IRAS had investigated or audited about 71,000 claims or around 30% of the PIC cash payout claims made from years of assessment 2011 to 2015.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He suggested that IRAS audit and investigate more PIC claims.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: IRAS takes a risk-based approach in its enforcement, and this 30% is not a fixed rule.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The 71,000 claims were identified for investigation or audit based on the use of analytics and risk profiling, as well as the experience of the IRAS investigators.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Hence, there was no need for a clawback.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: About 5,500 claims are undergoing audit or investigation.
